dct_description_sm: We sampled carbon and nitrogen stable isotope values of plant and beaver tissues in Wemindji territory for three main reasons. The first intention was to determine whether freshwater and terrestrial plants could be differentiated by their isotopic signatures. The second reason was to estimate the seasonal freshwater and terrestrial contributions in the diets of beavers using the stable isotope ratios of beaver fur and teeth. The general purpose was to examine freshwater and terrestrial ecosystem linkanges. This work examined ecosystem linkages as part of a SSHERC CURA (Community University Research Alliance) project aiming at the creation of a culturally appropriate protected in the Paakumshumwaau and Maatuskaau watersheds.
dct_subject_sm: Social sciences, economics and policy -> Traditional Ecological Knowledge (TEK)
dct_title_s: Carbon and nitrogen stable isotope values of aquatic and terrestrial plants, beaver teeth, and beaver fur in Wemindji Territory, James Bay, Quebec
